interfaceCtat.descricao: Interface FIXA do tutor (a mesma tela para todos os problemas): enunciado; DUAS retas numéricas de 0 a 1, uma para cada quantidade (rotuladas "Amount Kewana painted" e "Amount Adam painted"); para cada reta há um campo onde o aluno digita em quantas partes iguais dividi-la (com confirmação) e, depois, marca o ponto da fração correspondente; abaixo, um seletor em que o aluno escolhe UMA destas alternativas: "Kewana painted more fence."; "Adam painted more fence."; "Both painted same amount of fence."; botão Hint; botão Done. Os passos do aluno são ações NESSES componentes (dividir cada reta, marcar cada ponto, escolher a alternativa, concluir).

dicas.texto: What does the denominator tell you about the number of equal parts?
Use the denominator of Kewana's fraction as the number of equal parts on her number line.
Kewana's fraction is 2/3, so enter the denominator in the first number-of-parts field.
Type the number that appears below the fraction bar in 2/3, then confirm the division.
How many equal parts from 0 does the numerator tell you to count?
Start at 0 and count the equal intervals one at a time toward 1.
There are 3 equal intervals, and the target is reached after counting 2 of them from 0.
Click the second division mark after 0 on Kewana's three-part number line.
Which part of Adam's fraction tells you how many equal sections the whole needs?
Read Adam's denominator and use it as the number of equal parts on his number line.
Adam's fraction is 4/7. Enter the number below the fraction bar in the second number-of-parts field.
Type Adam's denominator into the field for his number line, then confirm it.
What does the numerator tell you to count on Adam's divided number line?
Begin at 0 and count the equal intervals toward 1 until you reach the numerator's count.
Adam's line has 7 equal intervals. Count 4 intervals from 0.
Click the fourth division mark after 0 on Adam's seven-part number line.
On number lines with the same endpoints, which fraction represents more: the point farther left or the point farther right?
Compare both marked positions between 0 and 1 instead of comparing only the numerators or denominators.
Look carefully at the two points and identify which one is closer to 1.
Choose the student whose marked point is farther right on the number line.
What should you do after selecting the comparison supported by the two number lines?
Check that a comparison choice is selected before submitting the completed problem.
Review the selected comparison and locate the button used to submit the finished problem.
When the correct comparison is selected, activate the button labeled Done.

exercicio.statement:
Kewana and Adam are earning money by painting both sides of a fence. When it was lunch time, they decided to compare who has painted more since they started. Use the number line to find out which student has painted more of the fence.
Kewana has painted 2/3 of one side of the fence.
Adam has painted 4/7 of the other side of the fence.
Who has painted more fence?
